checks.group: Existing seven-step ticket and AgentOps smoke
checks.observed: Logged in, previewed the ticket, checked search_kb and classify_ticket records and pending approval, explicitly confirmed, then checked the created ticket, successful create_ticket record and AgentOps metrics.
Repeating a successful confirmation returned HTTP 400. The ticket count stayed at one for that tenant.
Confirmation with a modified title returned HTTP 400. Cancellation recorded the logged-in decision actor and set cancelled. Later confirmation returned HTTP 400. The ticket count stayed unchanged.
Rejection recorded the logged-in decision actor and set rejected. Later confirmation returned HTTP 400. The ticket count stayed unchanged.

Cross-tenant run, trace, tool-call and approval reads, confirm, reject and cancel returned HTTP 404. Ticket detail also returned HTTP 404 across tenants in both directions. A tenant ID supplied in the preview body had no effect. Confirmation with a JWT from the matching tenant returned HTTP 201 and recorded that tenant and actor on the ticket.
Preview returned no draft or approval, did not request ticket creation and left the ticket count unchanged.
Each tenant listed only its own runs and one ticket. The run counts were four and one, with one approved approval per tenant. An unauthenticated AgentOps run-list request returned HTTP 401.

ticket_creation: Two explicit confirmations created the only two fictional tickets, one per tenant. Preview did not write a ticket.

focused_regression.scope: Six existing Ticket CRUD, Ticket Agent and AgentOps test modules in a separate offline process with a temporary database. Included single-winner SQLite regression cases for confirm racing confirm, reject or cancel.

evidence_scope: Public aggregate of the local execution record. Hashes identify the archived artifacts. The 2026-10-27 source-scope real-provider acceptance is a separate run.
out_of_scope: Real-provider RAG-to-ticket behavior, retrieval or answer quality, and autonomous model planning

Same-tenant requester-bound approval and a support/admin role requirement on Ticket Agent confirm. Confirm uses login and JWT tenant scope. AgentOps reject and cancel have their own support/admin role gate.
Production IAM, production throughput, public deployment and persistent service restart
Cross-transaction exactly-once ticket and audit writes, crash recovery and storage failure coverage
